correctness.rationale: In the general component theorem, each prime extension lies in exactly one occupied component or creates a new singleton component. Induction establishes both necessity and sufficiency for the occupied local-rank bounds and the decreasing ladder of unused component ranks; principal kernels then transfer componentwise. For strict chain components, the local gap rank is floor(log2(gap+1)), giving the exact marked-position formula, minimum size, unique kernel, and r+1 next-order extremal types. A separate direct-game finite checker agrees on 66,963 marked configurations through ten vertices at rank thresholds zero through four; finite checks do not prove unbounded ranks. A second actual-game checker for graph components (not strict chains) agreed with the general theorem on 838 marked host configurations through rank three; no infinite assertion relies on computation.

value.rationale: A general structural rank-composition law permits calculations and induced-embedding principal kernels to transfer from any hereditary finite relational class with a unique singleton to disjoint equivalence-partitioned components. Its strict-chain application resolves every finite marked rank, produces a universal exponential staircase kernel, sharp smallest host and r+1 next-smallest types with labelled counts. The interaction of internal interval capacities and external independent-component resources gives a motivated reusable invariant rather than a one-off table.
